code.why: The host process around the fetch: a listener a deployment starts (runtime contract R12b). The life and the examples walk the pack's fetch on an in-memory World, with no listener.

A slash command or an interaction a person's client asks of a Socket Mode app, through the World's command and action doors, waits on the door's request for the app's acknowledgement on its open connection (https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/using-socket-mode, "Acknowledge events"). A walk takes one step at a time, so a socket step could send the acknowledgement only after the asking door had already answered: only a live Socket Mode client beside the door (Slack's own @slack/socket-mode, as an app runs it against a World) reaches it.
